item.title: Bournemouth hit with double injury blow ahead of Sparta Prague visit
item.description: Bournemouth hit with double injury blow ahead of Sparta Prague visit Marco Rose has confirmed Juanlu Sánchez and Alex Tóth will be absent for prolonged periods after suffering injuries. Juanlu sustained an ankle injury while featuring for the under-21s, with the Cherries still evaluating the extent of the ligament damage. Tóth has had surgery on a hamstring injury sustained in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win over AC Milan in October, with the Hungarian midfielder not expected back until after the new year. Ahead of his side’s clash against Sparta Prague, Rose confirmed the plans to replace the 21-year-old with Eli Junior Kroupi in their next European squad, after the Frenchman’s own return from injury. “Juanlu twisted his ankle in the under-21s game,” Rose said. “It’s a ligament injury and we’re still assessing how to manage it and how long he will need. “Alex has had his surgery and everything went well. We’re not going to see him before the new year. We’re going to miss him for several months. Kroupi will be in the next European squad. We have some decisions to make with Alex Tóth missing and potentially moving players around in line with the European rules. “We communicated it very clear when we decided to do it like we do it now. We said Junior is injured more than 60 days and we said if Junior is back we are going to have Premier League games and cup games. “We made the decision to change him after four games in the European so after the next game he will be available.” Bournemouth sit fourth in the league phase of the Europa League after winning all three of their matches so far.

item.title: Jack Campbell gives injury update after being hospitalized on Nov. 1
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell said he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body after suffering a scary-looking injury against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. The former Iowa football player addressed his injury for the first time in a statement released by the Lions on Wednesday, Nov. 4, three days after he was hospitalized following a tackle on former Hawkeye and Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express," Campbell wrote. Jack Campbell gives injury update On the first play of the fourth quarter in the Lions' 19-15 win, Campbell's head appeared to hit Hockenson's left hip as he made the tackle. Campbell remained motionless on the field for more than 10 minutes and was loaded onto a cart and taken off the field. The incident silenced the crowd at Ford Field as players and staff from both teams took a knee, with some Lions players visibly shaken and fighting back tears for their teammate. "To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you," Campbell wrote on Wednesday. "This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people." The Cedar Falls native expressed gratitude to the Lions' medical staff and the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit. "I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you." Campbell, who turned 26 in August, did not elaborate on the extent of his injury in his statement. During his Nov. 4 news conference , Lions coach Dan Campbell spoke briefly about the linebacker's recovery, saying it was "powerful" to hear the update from Campbell and that his status is changing every 8-10 hours, "in a good way." "There's no easy way to do this, but we have to acknowledge it. Let's talk about it, and make sure [the players] know. But I also know that they're not postponing this game," the Lions coach said. "The only way to really honor Jack, and what he wants, is to make sure that we're locked in and ready to go." The Lions take the field again Sunday, Nov. 8 against the Miami Dolphins at 12 p.m. CT. item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy has dropped a bombshell claim regarding the true intentions of LIV Golf during this year’s Masters Tournament. The four-time major champion stated that officials from the Saudi-backed league were actively circulating a message at Augusta National Golf Club that they aimed to dismantle the European Tour. This revelation comes just days after news broke that the Saudi Public Investment Fund was pulling its financial support from the struggling league. The comments highlight the aggressive tactics used during the height of the golf civil war, suggesting the financial arms race was designed to eliminate a specific competitor rather than just build a new one. McIlroy’s comments were made while he was competing at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. He explicitly backed the statements made by DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings. Kinnings had told The Scotsman earlier in the week that LIV Golf used its massive financial muscle to target events and sponsors with the goal of destroying the European circuit. McIlroy told reporters, “I agree with everything that Guy said.” He elaborated on the situation, noting that the disruption went beyond just taking players and sponsors. “They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race,” McIlroy said. The specific claim about the Masters remains the most startling part of his assessment, as it places the conflict directly on the grounds of the sport’s most prestigious event. The Masters Revelation and Financial Reality The core of McIlroy’s argument centers on the idea that LIV Golf’s presence was never about sustainable growth but rather about market dominance through destruction. According to Today’s Golfer , McIlroy said that LIV Golf officials were “going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy the European Tour”. This statement aligns with the broader narrative that the Saudi funding was temporary and conditional on a return on investment. McIlroy believes the investors eventually realized they would not get that return or decided to leave the golf space entirely to invest in something more profitable. He described the era as a “very strange time” that the golf world will look back on. The funded International Series on the Asian Tour departed the circuit “high and dry” concerning long-term results before eventually partnering with the PGA Tour and The European Tour, having been cited as a short-term example of proper money use. McIlroy argues that this outcome was inevitable. While the financial war raged, the DP World Tour has had to navigate the complex issue of players trying to return. item.title: Tee Higgins wins his first AFC Offensive Player of the Week award
item.description: Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against the Tennessee Titans . It is Higgins' first career AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards in the victory. He caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . Higgins has 726 receiving yards this season, second only to Seattle Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Higgins is averaging 103.7 receiving yards per game. Burrow and Higgins were nominated for FedEx Air & Ground Players of the Week. After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. item.title: 76ers Must Ignore Celtics’ Paul George Jaylen Brown Noise
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics are already acting like they won the trade before the season even gets hot. Fans on the other side are pushing a narrative that Jaylen Brown is simply better than Paul George right now. This is a dangerous trap for Philadelphia to fall into, and the 76ers need to shut down that talk immediately. The numbers show a different story when you look at the full picture rather than just the first few weeks. The Real Numbers Don’t Lie It is easy to get caught up in the current standings. The Sixers sit at the top of the Eastern Conference with a 7-1 record, while the Celtics are 5-2. Per The Sixer Sense , the team in Boston wants fans to believe they got the better end of the deal by swapping players. They point out that Brown is putting up 20.6 points per game while shooting 41.9% from deep in his first seven games. George averaged 16.7 points and 37.5% field-goal shooting while in Philadelphia. But those small sample sizes do not tell the whole truth about the contract or the history. The front office in Philly paid $211 million for a nine-time All-Star who missed more than half the games over the last two seasons. Just last year, Brown earned All-NBA honors and MVP consideration while playing for the Celtics. That pedigree matters more than a few weeks of early-season stats. The Sixers paid for a star, and they cannot let a short slump define the entire trade. The LeBron Factor Changes Everything The 76ers landed Brown, and everything suddenly changed in the race for a superstar. Per The Sixer Sense , James is far and away Philly’s best facilitator and most influential presence right now. He joined the team as part of the swing for Brown. Before this swap, the Sixers were not even in the running for the veteran guard. Rumors had him heading to the Golden State Warriors, Cleveland Cavaliers, or Miami Heat instead. Absent that move, the squad would have likely returned with a roster incapable of advancing past the second round. The Celtics have not yet played the Sixers, with the first matchup scheduled for November 10. The regular season does not end until April 11, so there is plenty of time for the real story to unfold. Both teams have strong starts, but the Sixers hold a 1.5-game lead over Boston in the standings. George is bought into the system in Boston, but the foundation in Philadelphia is built on something much bigger than a few games of stats. The 76ers must ignore the noise and focus on the long haul.

item.description: Jodie Burrage has been ranked as high as 85th in the world and represented Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup [Getty Images] Britain's Jodie Burrage has been receiving support from WTA staff at an event in India after being sent death threats on social media. Burrage, 27, was bombarded with abusive online messages when she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles main-draw match in 16 months on Tuesday. On Wednesday, she won in the last 16 of the Chennai Open doubles alongside Robin Montgomery of the United States. "Protecting players and the wider tennis family from online threats and abuse is a key priority for the WTA," the governing body told BBC Sport. "We have WTA staff on the ground in Chennai offering Jodie support, along with our wider player welfare and Threat Matrix team." Burrage shared a story on her Instagram account that showed the direct messages she had been sent following a 3-6 6-3 7-5 loss to India's Vaishnavi Adkar. "Nice welcome back to tour. The WTA insists it is taking a "proactive approach" to protecting female players from abuse. The Threat Matrix system, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, can identify people behind the accounts that threaten players, enabling investigations to take place and potentially leading to legal action. Female players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to data from the service. "This includes reporting abusive content for removal, escalating serious cases to law enforcement and supporting action to prevent real-world harm. "As much of the abuse players receive comes through direct messages, the WTA has offered Jodie additional support. item.description: ‘Not good’ – Ally McCoist slams Liverpool star after mistake which left teammate ‘livid’ Ally McCoist was critical of one Liverpool player for his unwitting role in Fenerbahce’s equaliser against the Reds in the first half of their Champions League game on Wednesday. The away side took a well-deserved lead in the 25th minute when Trey Nyoni’s deflected shot sailed into the net, with the teenage midfielder being credited with his first official goal in senior football. However, the hosts restored parity just four minutes later, and again it was with the aid of a deflection as Mason Greenwood’s free kick hit off Jeremy Jacquet and was diverted into the net, with Alisson Becker not disguising his rage at the defensive wall in front of him. McCoist slams Jacquet over Fenerbahce equaliser Speaking on co-commentary for TNT Sports (via BBC Sport ), McCoist called out the French defender for turning his back on the ball as the set piece was struck. The Scotsman said: “I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall. Alisson is livid. Jeremy Jacquet turns his back. You have to stand up and take it. Not good defending.” (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust A moment that Jacquet will want to forget The summer arrival from Rennes has been excellent in his time at Liverpool so far, rightly receiving plenty of praise for his performances and winning his first senior call-up for France, but he won’t be happy with his part in Greenwood’s rather fortuitous equaliser. The normally teak-tough 21-year-old paid a heavy price for turning his back on the ball, even if nobody could legislate for the huge stroke of luck that Fenerbahce received. item.title: Real Sociedad slam referees in official statement
item.description: Real Sociedad slam referees in official statement Real Sociedad does not accept the technical explanation offered by the Technical Committee of Referees (CTA). Following the controversial Basque derby against Athletic Club, the San Sebastián club issued a strongly worded official statement flatly rejecting the suggestion that the penalty awarded against Jon Mikel Aramburu was merely an “IT incident.” For the 'txuri-urdin' club, what happened at San Mamés was a structural breakdown in officiating caused by three consecutive acts of negligence that decisively altered the result. In its statement, the club sets out the sequence of errors in detail. The first failure, Real Sociedad alleges, occurred on the pitch: a clear error of judgment by the referee, who awarded the penalty without noticing that Aramburu had touched the ball before making any contact with his opponent. The second failing concerns the video operation room (VOR). The club maintains that there was a blatant failure to follow the review protocol: the video officials failed to identify that earlier touch despite having television footage that clearly showed it. The third failure involved Connected Ball technology. Real Sociedad cites the CTA's own acknowledgment of a delay of between one and two frames (20 to 40 milliseconds) in the smart ball's signal, but stresses that this technical anomaly threw the system out of calibration and misled the video officials. Rather than limiting its complaint to dissatisfaction with the match's outcome, the club has directly challenged the refereeing authorities with three key questions about the procedure: What verification protocol was followed in the VOR before confirming the foul? Who bears technical responsibility for calibrating the ball's sensor and ensuring it is synchronized? What oversight checks are in place to detect millisecond discrepancies before making a match-deciding decision? Real Sociedad concludes its statement with a stark warning: formal apologies do not undo the sporting damage. The club is demanding an urgent, comprehensive review of technological protocols to restore credibility to a system that, after the events in Bilbao, has been called into serious question. In the UEFA Champions League however, Leipzig have suffered two defeats at the hands of Como and Real Madrid - both 4-1 scorelines away from home - as well as a narrow 1-0 win at home to PSV. Manchester City continue to face competitive duties without the availability of Antoine Semenyo, who is expected to be sidelined and unavailable for action until mid-December owing to an injury. item.title: Red Wings Shuffle Goalies With John Gibson’s Status Unclear
item.description: The Red Wings goalie picture moved again Wednesday. Detroit reassigned Carter Gylander from the ECHL’s Toledo Walleye to the Grand Rapids Griffins, one day after John Gibson left a 4-2 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning with a lower-body injury . Gibson stopped 11 of 13 shots before he exited after the first period. What does that mean for Detroit? Oct 31, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender John Gibson (36) makes a save in the third period against the St. Louis Blues at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) What the Red Wings Goalie Shuffle Signals With Gylander moving up to Grand Rapids, we can piece together what this means for Detroit. Especially after Gibson left the game hurt, the read is that a goalie from Grand Rapids is headed the other way. Gibson is still on the Red Wings roster , but he is also on the injury status list . Detroit has not officially announced a call up, and we can assume one is coming before the Red Wings host the Vegas Golden Knights on Thursday, Nov. 5 at 7 p.m. ET. Our Current Backup Goalie Daniil Tarasov is the backup to Gibson, and he has played well this season in a small sample. Tarasov faced 13 shots against Tampa and saved 12 of them , giving the Red Wings a chance to stage a comeback. Coach Todd McLellan told reporters he did not have an update on Gibson after the game, but he was clear about where Tarasov stands. “Anytime we’ve called his number, he’s come in and played really well. Obviously, with Gibby getting injured … he’s going to get more playing time, and we’ll see where he goes with it.” Todd McLellan, via Detroit Hockey Now Oct 20, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender Daniil Tarasov (80) watches play behind the net against the Seattle Kraken during the second period at Climate Pledge Arena. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tarasov has played six games this season with a .927 save percentage and a 1.74 goals-against average . Among goalies with at least five appearances, he is tied for second in save percentage with Igor Shesterkin and sits third in goals-against average . The company comes with a caveat. Shesterkin played only five games before a season-ending knee injury , and six games is a short run for Tarasov, so those numbers may even out as the season goes. The Most Likely Call Up Michal Postava is the most likely candidate. He has been a brick wall for Grand Rapids and was named AHL Goaltender of the Month for October. His first NHL start came against the Edmonton Oilers, where he held up against Connor McDavid and won the game in a shootout . With the Griffins this season, Postava is 5-0-0 with a .955 save percentage and a 1.20 goals-against average . He would be the smart choice to back up Tarasov, though maybe Trey Augustine gets his NHL debut instead.

item.title: Real Madrid devise special training plan to help struggling superstar rediscover his best form
item.description: Real Madrid devise special training plan to help struggling superstar rediscover his best form Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr. was among the most feared attackers in Europe for several seasons. He had a stellar 2023/24 season that earned him second place in the Ballon d’Or, but ever since, his career has seemingly gone downhill. No longer the player he once was, the Brazilian’s lack of efficiency has become a major problem for Real Madrid. Despite his poor form, Los Blancos continue to back him, believing he will return to his best sooner rather than later. Jose Mourinho has made it a priority to help the 26-year-old regain his best form in the coming months. Mourinho determined to bring back the best version of Vinicius According to Mario Cortegana of The Athletic , Vinicius is fully aware that his performances have fallen below his usual standards. Personal difficulties, including a break-up with his girlfriend, have affected him during an already challenging period. Real Madrid are waiting for Vinicius Jr. to get back to his best. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) While this has been reflected in his performances on the pitch, Mourinho continues to rate the Brazilian extremely highly. Real Madrid’s coaching staff have designed a special training programme aimed at restoring the winger’s explosiveness, acceleration and physical sharpness. Vinicius is also said to be working to maintain his fitness during his four-match domestic suspension, which kept him out of El Clasico . His situation has not been helped one bit by Yan Diomande’s impressive performances on the left wing in his absence. The summer signing has settled in very well at Real Madrid and brought much better balance to the team, especially defensively. Vinicius still has Mourinho’s full backing Nevertheless, Mourinho believes the Brazilian can regain the level that helped Madrid win two Champions League titles. Real Madrid are fully behind Vinicius Jr. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) That confidence is significant. Vinicius has faced increasing criticism this season, but the manager understands that few players possess his ability to change matches through individual brilliance. Even during his suspension, the manager has made sure to start the Brazilian in Champions League games to give him continuity. For Real Madrid, this shouldn’t become a situation where they have to choose between Vinicius and Diomande. However, the Brazilian will have to do more than just show intent to get back to his best. He needs to find a way to contribute more to the team. It will be interesting to see whether the specialised programme the coaching staff have put him on can help Vinicius get back to his best. A sharp and in-form Vinicius would make this Real Madrid team even more difficult to face, and it remains to be seen how Mourinho handles this situation.

item.title: Campbell has full lower body movement after neck injury
item.description: Jack Campbell was drafted by the Detroit Lions in 2023 [Getty Images] Detroit Lions player Jack Campbell has confirmed he has full movement in his lower body and is progressing with his upper body after sustaining a neck injury. Campbell was taken to hospital after he was struck in the head during the Lions' NFL game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. The Lions released a statement on social media on behalf of 26-year-old linebacker Campbell, saying that he is "very optimistic". "I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time," the statement said. "I have full movement in my lower body and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive and focusing on getting better." Campbell also thanked coaches and medical staff for their care, as well as the messages of support that he and his family have received. He also said that the city is "built on toughness, resilience and grit" which will be his attitude towards his recovery. Campbell was taken from the pitch on a stretcher after he hit his head while tackling tight end TJ Hockenson in the fourth quarter. He received medical assistance before being removed from the field, having been lying face down on the ground.
